transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess the main thing is… my wife’s been noticing it more than me, maybe. She’ll be telling me something, like about my cousin’s appointments or who needs a ride where — there’s been a lot of that kind of coordinating lately — and I’ll be looking right at her, nodding along, you know. But then a minute later I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she said.

It’s embarrassing, because it’s not like I don’t care. I’m sitting there, I’m trying to listen. But somehow it just doesn’t stick, and then she has to repeat it. That’s really what pushed me to come in.
Have you had this kind of trouble taking in what people say ever since you were younger?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, it’s funny, I don’t remember it as a “problem” exactly back then, but my parents used to get those comments from teachers in grade school — that I was bright, but always off daydreaming somewhere.

I’d leave homework in my desk, or I’d start classwork and then need reminders to actually finish it. This was pretty young, definitely before middle school — before I was 12. At the time I think everybody just kind of said, “Oh, that’s how he is,” you know?
Do these attention lapses cause problems for you at work?

Well, I’m not really in a regular job now, so “work” is a little different. But I do help with some catering things here and there, small jobs, and that’s where it can show up. I’ll have to double-check myself or redo something because I mixed up a detail.

And at home it’s been more of a problem lately, honestly. With my cousin’s care, rides and appointments and all that, my wife feels like she can’t totally count on me to keep it straight. That’s caused some tension. I mean, she’s handling a lot too, so I get why she’s frustrated.
Do you notice the same kind of trouble paying attention when you’re doing things on your own, not just when your wife is talking to you?

Yeah, yeah, it’s not just with her. Like if I sit down to work out one of those catering orders, I’ll start out fine — checking the quantities, dates, that kind of thing — and then suddenly I’m thinking about something totally else, like whether I remembered to call somebody back, or even some random thing from church.

Same with parish planning calls. I’ll be listening and maybe taking notes, and then a few minutes later I’m looking at what I wrote and it’s like… did I even read this? I have to go back over the same notes again like it’s the first time. It’s not constant, but it happens enough that I notice it.
Do you ever forget important recent events completely, even after someone reminds you about them?

I don’t think completely, no. I mean… if someone reminds me, usually it comes back, at least enough that I go, “Oh right, yeah.” Sometimes it takes a minute.

Like, my wife might say, “Remember we talked about that?” and I’m sort of blank at first, which is embarrassing. But then once she gives me the context — where we were, what day it was, that sort of thing — I usually remember. It’s more like I didn’t hold onto it well, not like it’s totally gone.
When your mind drifts, is it usually because you’re getting caught up in worry?

Not usually worry, no. I mean, sometimes there’s stuff on my mind, like anybody, but a lot of the time it’s just… I drift.

Like with a catering order, I’ll sit down and I’m doing it, I’m looking at the quantities or the notes, and then before long I realize I’ve been thinking about something else entirely. Or on a parish planning call, I’ll be listening, and then I look back at my notes and it’s like I never really took them in. Then I have to go over it again.

So it’s not always because I’m anxious. It just sort of wanders off on its own.
Besides at home, have these attention problems caused difficulties in other parts of your life, like school, work, church, or relationships?

Yeah… mostly at home, honestly, but it does spill over some.

With my wife, it’s caused tension because of helping with my cousin’s care. She’ll feel like she can’t quite count on me to track what I’m supposed to track, and I don’t blame her, but it doesn’t feel great. And then with catering stuff — I’m not doing big full-time work or anything, but when I help with those orders, I’ve had to double-check myself or redo little parts so things don’t get mixed up.

It’s funny, because years ago I used to keep all kinds of things straight, like parish events, food lists, who needed what — well, maybe I only remember it that way. But now even small jobs, I’ll go back over them just to make sure I didn’t miss something. So yes, it’s not only at home, but home is where it shows up the most.
Have these attention problems gotten noticeably worse as you’ve gotten older?

Yeah, I’d say it has, but more in the last year than just “getting older” in general.

It’s been noticeably harder for about… 11 months, I guess, since my cousin moved in with us after surgery. That changed the whole rhythm of the house, and there’s more to keep track of. Before that I had moments, sure, but this past almost-year is when it really started standing out to me.

I don’t know if that’s age or just the situation, but that’s the timing I notice.
Because of these attention or memory problems, have you needed other people to take over things you used to manage on your own?

Not fully take over, I guess… but my wife has had to step in more, especially with my cousin’s care. Like, she’ll remind me what needs to be tracked or she’ll just handle something herself because she’s not sure I’ll keep it straight. That’s caused some tension, honestly.

And with the catering things, nobody’s exactly taking it away from me, but I’ve had to double-check myself or redo little pieces so I don’t mix up a small order. Funny, because I used to be the one people handed lists to at church dinners and things like that—anyway, now I don’t trust it as much unless I go back over it.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak?

Um… finding words? Not really, I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes I’ll pause, but that’s more me losing the thread of what I was saying than not knowing the word, if that makes sense.

My wife might say I go around the barn to explain something — I’ve always kind of done that, especially if I’m telling a story and then I remember some other piece of it. But I haven’t noticed, like, reaching for simple words and not being able to get them. Not that stands out to me.
Have you been getting lost or turned around in places that should feel familiar to you?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ll take a wrong turn now and then, but not in places I know. If I’m going to the grocery store or church or around our neighborhood, I’m fine.

Sometimes parking lots get me turned around for a second — but that’s always been true, especially those big ones where every row looks the same. But getting lost somewhere familiar? No, I haven’t noticed that.
As a child, were you also often disorganized or forgetful with everyday things, like losing school materials or forgetting assignments?

Yeah… that does go back pretty far, actually. In grade school, before I was 12, I remember teachers telling my parents I was bright, but I was always kind of off in my own head — daydreaming, you know.

And I’d leave homework sitting in my desk or forget to turn things in. Sometimes I had done the work, but it just didn’t make it where it was supposed to go. Teachers had to remind me to finish classwork too. My mother used to get frustrated because she’d say, “If you can understand it, why can’t you just hand it in?” That sort of thing.
Are you having trouble managing your medications?

A little, yeah. Not like I’m taking the wrong thing all the time, but I can start something simple — like setting up my cousin’s pill organizer — and then later realize I left one or two steps unfinished.

It’s the same kind of thing if I’m cleaning up after cooking, like wiping down the prep table, and then I notice I didn’t actually finish part of it. So with medications, I try to be careful, but the follow-through is where I can slip.
Compared with a year or two ago, do you feel your attention and memory are clearly worse than they used to be?

Yeah… I’d say it’s been more noticeable, but not like my whole life suddenly changed overnight. It’s been, maybe, about 11 months or so — since my cousin moved in with us after her surgery.

At first I thought it was just the house being busier, because when someone new is there, you know, their routines and appointments and all the extra stuff kind of take over. And she had all these things she needed help with, and I’d be trying to keep track of what was mine and what was hers. But since then, yeah, I’ve noticed it’s been harder than it used to be.
Has anyone besides your wife told you that your attention or memory seems worse than it used to be?

Um… besides my wife? I’m not sure anyone’s said it that plainly. I mean, people might repeat something or kind of look at me like, “Did you forget?” but I don’t know if that’s them noticing a change or just normal family stuff.

My wife is the one who really brings it up. Other people… I can’t think of anyone specific who’s told me it’s worse than before.
Has anyone who knows you well said they’ve noticed your thinking or memory has clearly declined compared with a year ago?

Not really, no. I mean, my wife is the one who says things, but someone else who knows me well saying, “You’ve clearly declined since last year”? I can’t think of anybody.

Sometimes family notices little things, but then we’ll be talking about groceries or my cousin’s appointments or whatever and it’s hard to know if they mean anything by it. So… no, not that clearly.
Have you had any memory or thinking tests done, and were you told the results were below normal for your age?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve done regular doctor visits where they ask you questions, and sometimes there’s forms or little screenings, but I don’t remember anyone sitting me down for, like, a memory test and then telling me, “This is below normal for your age.”

Unless you mean something specific, like those puzzles or word recall things? I don’t think I’ve had that done, or at least nobody explained results to me that way.
Because of these changes, are you still able to manage your finances on your own?

Yeah, I mean… for the most part I think I can still handle that. Bills and money stuff, I don’t think that’s where I’ve had the biggest trouble.

It’s more like lately I’ll forget things I meant to do, like calling the doctor’s office back, or I’ll mean to pick up a prescription and then it just slips. Or I’m supposed to leave for one of my cousin’s appointments and then suddenly I’m running late because I got caught up in something else. My cousin’s got a lot of appointments, so there’s always some time or place to keep straight.

But finances… I think I’m still managing those on my own.
Do you now need your wife to manage your medications for you?

No, she doesn’t manage them for me. I mean, not like she’s laying them out or anything. I do forget sometimes—like I’ll mean to pick up a prescription and then I get sidetracked, or I’ll forget to call the doctor’s office back.

It’s kind of the same thing with my cousin’s appointments, too. I’ll know I need to leave at a certain time, and then suddenly I’m still in the house doing something else. But my wife isn’t managing my medications for me, no.
Has your wife told you that your attention or memory is clearly worse now than it was a year ago?

Yeah, she’s mentioned it. I don’t know if she’d say it exactly like “clearly worse,” but she’s definitely been pointing it out more.

It’s been, I guess, about 11 months now—since my cousin moved in with us after surgery. That kind of changed the whole rhythm of the house, you know, more stuff going on, more things to keep track of. My wife will say I’m not keeping up the way I used to, or she’ll notice I’m not as on top of things. So… yeah, compared to a year ago, I’d say she’s noticed it.
